title: Tenant + Route TTL matrix and compliance reporting for request payloads, traces, and aggregated metrics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define and implement a flexible TTL matrix and reporting automation that lets customers and internal teams set per-tenant and per-route retention policies for prompts, responses, request logs, traces, and derived metrics. This ticket covers policy model, Console UX, API surface, runtime enforcement contract, and automated compliance exports for audits.

Goals:
- Provide a TTL policy matrix UI and API allowing: default tenant-level TTL, route-level overrides, emergency legal-hold, and temporary extensions.
- Distinguish storage modes: live short-term storage, compressed archival, and governed exportable evidence bundles.
- Implement metrics retention tiers: raw request events (short), 1m/5m/1h aggregates (longer), and trend rollups (longest) to balance cost vs. queryability.
- Generate scheduled compliance reports and one-off evidence bundles scoped to tenant, date-range, and data categories (prompts/responses/metrics/logs).
- Ensure residency and KMS labeling metadata flows with retained objects for audit and export.

Scope in this ticket:
- Policy model and matrix definition (data types, default TTLs, allowed overrides).
- Console management screens and API endpoints for setting TTLs per tenant and per route.
- Report generation orchestration that produces time-bounded evidence bundles (zip + manifest) suitable for legal/compliance review.
- Enforcement contract for the serving/runtime/ingest teams with examples and integration tests.

Out of scope:
- On-prem installer changes (handled in Private deployment epic).
- Deep archival search UI (we'll expose exports; search over archives is follow-up).

Tradeoffs/Notes:
- Per-route TTLs increase metadata complexity (indexing cost) and query patterns; will need lightweight indexing to avoid perf regressions.
- Aggregating metrics for cost: keep raw events for <=30d by default, longer periods store only aggregates to preserve SLA for dashboards while controlling S3 cost.
- Legal-hold must be additive and not enable reads beyond policy; enforcement must block deletion workflows and be auditable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy data model document (Confluence) describing fields: data_type, default_ttl_days, max_override_days, route_allowlist, legal_hold_flag, residency_constraint.
- Console screen mockups for tenant and route TTL settings and a simple policy matrix view.
- Public API: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/data-lifecycle and PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/routes/{route}/data-lifecycle with validation and RBAC checks.
- Export endpoint or scheduled job that generates evidence bundles including manifests, checksums, and KMS key metadata.
- End-to-end test demonstrating policy enforcement: create request with route override, assert data deleted after TTL via background job simulation.
- Daily compliance report (CSV) summarizing active legal holds, overrides, and upcoming expirations for tenant admins.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: High cardinality of route-level policies causing lookup latency. Mitigation: fall back to hashed route namespace index and cache policy lookups in Redis with invalidation on change.
- Risk: Evidence exports accidentally include sensitive keys. Mitigation: export manifest includes pointer to encrypted blobs; export tooling runs KMS rewrap and redaction rules before bundling.

Open questions (needs PM+Eng design review):
1) Should we allow route wildcards or require explicit route IDs? (eng leaning: explicit only for early rollout).
2) What SLA do we provide for on-demand evidence exports? (goal: <30m for <10GB).
3) Legal-hold expiration semantics: require manual release or allow timed holds?

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize policy model and Confluence spec + Console wireframes (owner: PM).
- Week 2: Backend API schema + DB migration plan (owner: ENG storage).
- Week 3: Runtime enforcement hooks + caching layer and integration tests (owner: ENG runtime).
- Week 4: Console implementation + report generation job + initial e2e tests (owner: DX/Console + Eng).

Acceptance test examples and edge cases included in Confluence doc link below.
